english_verification.review_scope: Read the current English B02 country-history opening and representative native English mission localisation; confirmed the current English country name Corintar against localisation. Read actual fixed-revision history chunks for Corintar Order and Corin's Circle. Reviewed the translated body before the national-ideas appendix, pointer translations, heading levels, retained phase values, and relative links. Primary compared all native idea names/descriptions by actual current English localisation key. Source ranges may be locator envelopes; conditional and predecessor idea sets remain separate. No formal validators, tests, builds or browser checks were run.
unresolved: The Corintar Order and Corin's Circle Wiki pages provide organisational context, not a complete history of B02's later territorial holdings or current mission implementation.
Specific civilian casualties and event consequences of the Great Purge have not been verified event by event; the article does not infer a massacre from the mission title.
Comments about player recommendations and pacing are dated community opinions, not current guaranteed event timing.

rationale.campaign_length: The B02 tree defines 53 direct missions.
rationale.colonization: Frontier settlement offers some expansion, but overseas colonisation is not the main campaign.
rationale.complexity: Religious timing, chapters, and multi-stage mission prerequisites interact.
rationale.dark_story: The Great Purge, religious scrutiny, and reflection are central to the middle of the story.
rationale.difficulty: Religious progress and neighbouring politics affect the pace; this has not been tested in play.
rationale.diplomacy: The Empire, Gawed, and chapters of the faith across the region all require attention.
rationale.early_pressure: The adventuring company is trying to establish itself in a region shattered by the Greentide.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: The Corinite faith and religious visions shape the country's narrative.
rationale.narrative_density: Bluetusk, the chapters, the Great Purge, reconciliation, and orc equality form a complete conflict arc.
rationale.tall_play: Returning farmers and rebuilding cities and monasteries are important mission requirements.
rationale.trade_economy: Trade is present but secondary to reconstruction and religious politics.
rationale.warfare: The legacy of the Greentide and the unification of Escann are long-term military objectives.

identity.appearance: In 1444, an adventuring company formed by Corin's companions; the half-orc Lothane Bluetusk is its leader.
identity.formation_scope: B02 begins as an adventuring company and has a complete dedicated mission tree; the rise of Corinite faith and reconstruction do not themselves change its Tag.

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas and ambition only; optional idea groups and racial/government bonuses are excluded. Conditional alternatives are separate, not stacked. Adopting new ideas depends on the actual event/decision and player choice.

description.text: The old god of war Agrados was known for his ferocious rage and unyielding blows against his enemies, but Corin saw differently. She saw equal merit in using her powers not only to strike at her foes, but to use them to protect her faithful just the same - no such event can be compared to the Battle of Castonath when Corin raised her shield to defend Lothane Bluetusk from a killing blow by Korgus Dookanson himself, knowing that it would leave her exposed to Korgus' off-hand attack. Accepting her purpose, she used this moment of defense to return the favour and slew Korgus at the cost of her life, ending the Greentide once and for all.

description.text: Lothane Bluetusk was a loyal friend and companion of Corin and the first Grandmaster of the Corintar. While Corin's ideals started the Corintar, it was Lothane's work that organized the order into a legitimate force.

description.text: Corin. Lothane Bluetusk. Dominic of Gallowspeak. Eledas Silurion. All of these names and a dozen more of Corin's Circle have become household names across all of Cannor. We as their successors have big shoes to fill, but their heroism and legacy will never leave us.

description.text: Unlike others, we can claim no exalted lineage nor storied ancestry. We are merely honest men and women from a dozen races and cultures who came together because we believed in something and someone- Corin. Let us promote a new order based on ideals, not origins!

description.text: As more and more people were converted to the Corinite faith, more and more people felt the zeal that her will must be spread across all. This ever-growing group were known as the Corinite Crusaders, and warred across Cannor and even Anbennar itself hoping to bring justice to world.

description.text: When the old Corintar was disbanded and the affairs of the state were under control of the Corinite Crusaders, a new splinter group consisting of moderate Corinites formed a semi-secret society called the New Corintar. These members worked all across the world to secretly ensure that Corin's ideals of freedom, justice and good of man were upheld even beyond the borders of the Corintari state.

player_overview.avoid_if: Avoid it if you do not want to wait for religious phases and manage chapter requirements, or expect a spotless story about holy knights.
player_overview.how_it_plays: First reclaim and rebuild Escann as an adventuring company; organise chapters and undergo a religious turn in the middle game; later pursue reconciliation, oppose enslavement, and seek regional unification.
player_overview.overview: In 1444, Corintar is led by the half-orc Bluetusk and inherits the fame of Corin's struggle against the Greentide, but has not yet built a stable state. Bring farmers home, rebuild towns and monasteries, and establish chapters across Cannor; then a religious revival drives this sense of justice toward scrutiny and a Great Purge. Later reconciliation, orc equality, and anti-slavery missions force the country to confront its mistakes. This is a long Escanni epic with costly wars and religious prerequisites.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy character continuity, self-criticism, and a long religious and political turn in an Escanni campaign.
signature_features: Memories of Bluetusk and Corin's companions run through the company's state-building.
Transnational chapters, the rise of Corinite faith, and the Great Purge form a connected religious-political arc.
Later reconciliation, orc settlement, and opposition to enslavement test the ideals of the crusade.
player_overview.tagline: Lead the companions Corin left behind as they build an Escanni state willing both to fight and to question itself.

reasons: A continuous character story about Corin's companions and Bluetusk.
A strong turn from reconstruction through religious zeal to reconciliation.
Orc equality and opposition to enslavement have concrete mission support.
warnings: Religious phases and chapter missions may require waiting.
The middle of the campaign includes a Great Purge and coercive religious politics.

phase_scores.phase: The Great Purge and religious scrutiny
Chapter reconciliation and opposition to orcish enslavement

positive_indicators: Rebuilds farms and towns and trains their defenders.
Attempts reconciliation with chapters that left.
Promotes orc equality and an end to enslavement.
values.rationale: Returning people and rebuilding, monastic education, orc equality, and ending enslavement provide clear positive evidence. The administrative oath, purging chapters, and coercive religious scrutiny seriously weaken restraint. The casualties and details of the purge have not been checked event by event. War and religious propagation alone do not count against the score.
red_flags: Administrators must swear to use violence against those deemed faithless.
The Great Purge excludes dissenting chapters and triggers events.
